lead: nobody asked for it. it was built on the wednesday, it went across on the thursday, and the meeting that would have decided whether anyone wanted it never got called.
sun: The Hand starts before a commission arrives, since the interval in which one would be discussed is the interval in which the thing gets built. somebody says the word on a tuesday and by wednesday the jig exists, or the form, or the two paragraphs that end the argument, and it is in use before the week turns. nothing your hands have produced was ever picked from a list.
moon: getting there ahead of the request is the half you do without effort, and it never brings the other half with it — the case for the thing, the account of what it saved, the bill. a difficulty closed before anybody named it leaves nothing behind that could later be pointed at. the work is real and the trail of it is blank.
pull: you have never submitted a proposal in your life. every problem you solved was solved before the meeting about it, and a meeting that never happened leaves nothing behind.
tension: the ten things you made that nobody needed are the ones people can list, since an unwanted object sits on a desk for years and an averted mess sits nowhere. initiative is the warm reading of the habit and jumping the gun is the cold one, and both get said in the same month. when the year is assessed, the question is what you delivered against what was asked, and none of it was asked.
cost: a difficulty can be gone inside a day here, before it has a name or a budget line or a person whose fault it is, and almost nobody works that early. the same speed puts you outside every process that runs on requests, and standing, credit and the account of what you are for get assembled out of things somebody wanted done.

lead: you were eleven and you already knew why the house was going. what you did with knowing was get your brother out of it — the application, the fare, the sentence that made leaving thinkable.
sun: hands convert whatever they are given, so what you were holding went out of you sideways, as objects — a room found, a form filled in, a job heard about at the right hour. each of them carried a person out of that house without carrying any of the reason with it. four left on work you did, and the reason stayed exactly where it started.
moon: The Bearer's term never ended. what went in at eleven has not lost an ounce of itself, and the day for setting it down was always yours to choose and has never been chosen. each time your hands found a way to act on it without saying it, the pressure came down enough to hold another decade, so it was never told and not telling it was never decided.
pull: four people got out of that house on arrangements you made. what they were being got out of has never been said to any of them, and it was in you the whole time.
tension: in the family telling you are the one who never went anywhere: quiet, close to home, no push in you. your brother's leaving is his own story, he tells it well, and you are nowhere in it, because what you supplied looked like errands. correcting any of that means producing the thing underneath, thirty years late, to people who have built their lives on top of not having it. the two it would have helped are dead.
cost: three of your siblings have lives that were not available to them at seventeen, and each of those lives was assembled out of a fact none of them has heard. it stopped being useful around the sixth year and thirty more have gone by with it in there, so the only accurate account of that household sits in one place, unread, doing nothing for anybody in it.

lead: the form has one box for what you earn and your living arrives in seven pieces, none of them the main one, the biggest a different piece every couple of years, and nobody tells you when it changes.
sun: each of the seven is a thing you made exist and then let run: the small firm you got standing and left under another name, the trade you taught two people who now pass a fee back, the arrangement between two other parties that still routes a slice through you. none needed you after the first year, which is why there are seven. a start takes a season and then your hands are free.
moon: from any distance this reads as one number — a person doing all right, or a person who never made anything, depending which of the seven the other party has heard of. close up it separates into seven unrelated small incomes, six of them at rates other people fixed, and nobody who has dealt with you has had sight of more than two.
pull: no institution can read you. every bank, landlord and form wants the single figure, and the single figure is the one thing your life has never produced.
tension: a mortgage interview is where it stops being interesting. the man opposite needs employment or he needs a business, you have neither, and describing the actual thing honestly sounds like evasion in the exact places where it is most accurate. relatives run the opposite error and take you for comfortable, having heard of two of the seven and assumed the rest match. the year the biggest stopped, you learned its size from the hole it left.
cost: starting a thing that pays takes you about a season, with no capital in it, nothing but a want noticed and a push given, and there have been seven at an age when most people have managed none. it builds no position. seven starts is not a career, six of them are somebody else's property now, and the slice each returns was fixed verbally by them.

lead: same hour up, same distance covered, same thing left off the plate, thirty years without a gap — and the whole arrangement was copied off one body you stood beside for a single winter.
sun: you make habits in other people's bodies with no lesson anywhere in it: you turn up, you do the hour next to them, and by the fourth week their body has it and stops needing yours. people who trained beside you one season are still up at that hour, in towns you have never seen, each with an honest account of how they got there.
moon: what you hand across was never yours. it came off one man, whole, when you were nineteen, and has been kept at that grain since — the same hour, the same distance, the same refusal at the table. by any measure anybody could take now, you do it better than he ever did. nothing in you has run that comparison, and the standard has not been revised once.
pull: the hour runs in eleven bodies and began in none of them. you took it off one man, handed it on without a word about him, and kept no list of who has it.
tension: at the table it lands on other people: thirty years without one deviation is restful company to nobody, and two households have arranged their evenings around what you will not do. the harder part is interior. none of the regimen has been tried against your own body — what you go without was picked for somebody else's frame by a man who gave no reason, and whether you even want the thing you refuse has never been put to you.
cost: another person's body takes a permanent habit off you in a fortnight, with no instruction in it, and keeps it for the rest of their life, where coaches spend whole careers failing at that. your own has gone unexamined the entire time. thirty years of appetite settled at nineteen by watching somebody, and no stretch in it where you ate what you wanted and found out what that was.
